newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives make capital out of school tables.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives make capital out of school tables.

text.p: The government renewed its attack on Labour's education record on Tuesday as it published primary school performance tables showing the 10 worst-peforming local education authorities are controlled by Labour.

Launching what she called the biggest public information campaign since World War Two, Education Secretary Gillian Shephard said the tables provided further evidence that Labour LEAs were failing children and their parents.
She said the tables, which cover most of the 14,500 primary schools in England and are being published for the first time, showed that of the best 10 LEAs only one was run by Labour.
"Labour do not like the tables because they show Labour's policies to be based on the politics of envy not the excellence of education.
"They expose the appalling record of Labour in power and explode the myths they like to peddle," Shepherd told a news conference at Conservative central office.
Labour, whose leader Tony Blair has vowed to make education his number one priority if he wins the coming election, focused on the poor overall results.

Only a dozen or so schools had all their pupils come up to typical standards expected of 11-year-olds in English, maths and science. Forty percent of children nationally failed to come up to scratch, the tables showed.
Labour's education spokesman, David Blunkett, told BBC radio the tables showed the Conservatives' "incompetence" in addressing basics and teacher training during 18 years in power.
